plugins.description: One number per provider in the sidebar footer: how much of its capacity is used, and when it frees up.
plugins.overview:
See how much of each provider's capacity is in use, and when it frees up,
without opening anything.

## One number per provider

Pool Usage puts each connected provider's logo at the right end of the sidebar
footer with the share of its capacity in use right now: Claude and Codex,
every account in Account Pooler if you use it, and other providers that report
usage to BB, such as Cursor. Accounts weigh by the vendors' stated plan
multipliers, so a Max 20x seat counts twenty times a Pro seat. Codex Business
Pro Lite and Pro Lite each count as 5x Plus. The number turns red at 80%, or at
the percentage you pick in the plugin's only setting, **Red at, %**.

## When it frees up

Click a number for the provider's card, styled like the footer's `…` menu: the
total, the number of accounts when there are several, and up to four lines
showing when the total drops next and what it drops to.

## Resets

When Account Pooler's Claude or Codex accounts hold resets, which clear an
account's usage limits early, the card ends with a line such as
"Reset to 27% (3 available)": the total right after the reset that frees the
most capacity over the next week. Clicking it asks first, in BB's own dialog,
naming the account, when the reset expires, and the total before and after.
Only **Use reset** spends it.

## What it reads

The numbers refresh every 30 seconds. Pool Usage reads Account Pooler's
redacted account status and BB's provider usage readings. For resets, its
server uses the access tokens Account Pooler stores: it asks Anthropic and
OpenAI for them every 10 minutes and spends one only when you confirm it.
Tokens never reach the frontend, and the plugin never refreshes one.

plugins.description: Bookmark any chat message and jump back to it from a Bookmarks tab in the thread's right panel.
plugins.overview:
Save the answers worth coming back to, and get back to them in one click.

## Bookmark from the message

Every user and assistant message gets a **Bookmark** button in its action bar.
Click it and the message is saved; the button stays filled on that message, the
way a liked message looks, and clicking it again removes the bookmark with an
Undo. Select part of an assistant answer and choose **Bookmark** from the
selection menu to save just that passage as the bookmark's quote.

## A Bookmarks tab on the right

Open **Bookmarks** from the thread header, the side panel's new-tab actions, or
the quick palette (`Bookmarks: Show saved messages`). The tab lists every
bookmark, newest first, with its thread and when you saved it. Search matches
the saved text and thread titles in any case, and **This thread** narrows the
list to the open thread in timeline order.

Click a bookmark to jump straight to its message: bb opens the thread, scrolls
the timeline to the message, and flashes it, however far back it is. When the
message lives in another thread, the Bookmarks tab opens beside it so you can
keep browsing. Hover a bookmark to copy its full text or remove it.

## Local

Bookmarks live in the plugin's own SQLite database on your bb server. Each one
keeps a copy of the message text, so a bookmark stays readable after its thread
is deleted. Nothing is sent to an agent or an external service.

plugins.description: Superhuman-style speed for BB: keyboard shortcuts and search in any layout, threads you snooze until a time you pick or until their agent needs you, a layout for phones, and a quieter interface.
plugins.overview:
Superhuman-style speed for BB:

- **Shortcuts.** Shortcut hints on a held modifier; **/** searches, **H**
  snoozes, **E** archives, and numbers open a new thread's menus, in any
  keyboard layout.
- **Universal Search.** Find commands, threads, and snoozed threads using both
  the typed query and its English/Russian keyboard equivalent.
- **Snooze.** Hide a thread until a time you pick or until its agent needs you,
  from the moon in its header or any thread menu; **Show snoozed threads** lists
  them.
- **Archive Button.** Archive a thread from its header, next to Snooze.
- **Search Actions.** In thread search, **⌘↵** unsnoozes a snoozed thread or
  unarchives an archived one instead of opening it in split.
- **Dismiss Cards.** A close button on the cards above a thread's message box
  for background work, child threads, and the pull request; a card stays
  hidden in its thread until its words change.
- **Mobile Layout.** Bottom bars, edge swipes, and haptics on phones, with a
  fixed interface scale and pinch-to-zoom images. Thread titles stay hidden.
- **Hide Title Bar.** In the macOS desktop app, no top row with back, forward,
  and the sidebar button; their shortcuts still work.
- **UI Polish.** Icons in one tone and a thread bar without the external editor
  picker, with fixes for Safari's layout, for a Tesla's keyboard, and for inline
  visualizations in BB's iOS app.
- **Brief Replies.** Agents answer in few words of plain English, after Andrej
  Karpathy's advice, in threads started once it is on.

Shortcuts work on desktop, outside text fields, by key position, so **H** is
**H** in a Russian layout too. Snooze sits before Archive in every thread menu.
To snooze from a sidebar row in one click, add it in the row menu's
**Customize row actions**. Universal Search and Search Actions are verified for
BB 0.47.0 and 0.47.1 and turn themselves off on other versions. Settings have a
switch for each feature, all on by default except Hide Title Bar and Brief
Replies; turning Snooze off brings snoozed threads back.

## More San Francisco Plugins

Superhuman is one of the San Francisco Plugins, a family of BB plugins. The
others:

- **Bookmarks**: save any chat message and jump back to it from the thread's
  right panel.
- **Canvas**: images, text, and drawing in each thread, with screenshots your
  agent can read.
- **Annotate**: notes on the elements of a page in BB's Browser, sent to your
  agent with a screenshot.
- **Auto Update**: updates for the plugins you pick, installed every hour, day,
  or week.
- **Storage Cleaner**: what fills your Mac's disk, and cleanup of archived
  threads, worktrees, and caches.
- **Resource Monitor**: live CPU, RAM, and GPU bars for the BB server in the
  sidebar, with the numbers on hover.
- **San Francisco**: a quiet macOS-style theme after the Aside browser, with
  your pick of the eight macOS accent colors.
- **Pool Usage**: how much of each provider's capacity is in use and when it
  frees up, in the sidebar footer.

See all of them, with install steps, at
[github.com/rebryk/bb-plugins](https://github.com/rebryk/bb-plugins).

plugins.description: A quiet macOS-style theme after the Aside browser, with your pick of the eight macOS accent colors.
plugins.overview:
Make BB look like a calm, native Mac app, in the quiet style of the Aside
browser.

## A quiet window

The content sits on the gray window frame as one white card with soft corners.
Text uses the system font at 14 px, SF Pro on a Mac. Hierarchy comes from
shades of gray rather than lines: primary text is near black, and secondary
text a softer gray. Icons use a thinner stroke. Only the composer and what
floats above the page, such as menus, popovers, dialogs, toasts and the
command palette, cast a soft shadow. Dark mode follows the same rules, with a
near-black frame, a slightly lighter card and near-white text.

Text is at least as easy to read as in BB's default palette. Dark mode's card
is lighter than BB's, so its gray text, accent text and BB's terminal, diff,
status and code colors are brighter to match.

## Familiar places

In the sidebar, rows are a soft black and the open thread is a white pill.
Thread and panel headers lose their dividers. The composer gets larger corners,
a soft shadow and one round send button with an up arrow; Stop is the same
circle with a square. Above the composer, background work and child threads
each become one outlined card, and queued messages a sheet tucked behind the
composer. Right-panel tabs become quiet pills, and an empty new tab centers its
hint above outlined buttons.

## Settings like a document

Settings pages show a Settings › Page breadcrumb and a large page title. Section
headings are small caps, and a plugin's settings sit in the same white card as
BB's own. Selects shrink to their text and use a double chevron. Buttons, inputs
and badges are lighter, and menus and popovers are compact.

## One accent color

Pick one of the eight macOS accent colors: Blue, Purple, Pink, Red, Orange,
Yellow, Green or Graphite. It underlines links and colors file names, focus
rings, text selection, switches and checkboxes; everything else stays
neutral. Provider marks keep their shapes but take the surrounding text color.

## Turn it on

Choose San Francisco under Settings → Appearance → Palette, then click an
accent swatch under Settings → San Francisco. BB applies the palette before
the first paint and a non-Blue accent a moment later, once plugins load. Light
and dark follow BB's Theme setting. Choose Default to return to BB's look. No
external account or service is required.

plugins.description: A canvas in each thread for images, text, and drawing, with screenshots your agent can read.
plugins.overview:
Collect screenshots, write notes, and sketch feedback in each thread's Canvas.

## Images, notes, and drawing

Open **Canvas** in the thread's right panel. Paste a screenshot with **⌘V** /
**Ctrl+V**, drop an image, or choose **Add image**. Select, move, and resize
images; add text or yellow sticky notes; draw freehand or drag out an arrow.
Text grows as you type, with new lines only on **Enter**. Square sticky notes
wrap and fit their text automatically; resizing a note scales the text with it.
Double-click text or a note to edit within its selection frame. Hold **Shift**
for horizontal or vertical lines and arrows. Clicks and tiny movements do not
leave stray dots.
Colors and three visual size presets sit in the toolbar for one-click
selection. Drag annotations with a mouse in any tool; hold **Alt** / **Option**
to draw or write over them. Images move and
resize with **Select**, leaving the other tools free to annotate them.
Double-click an image with **Select** to crop it. Drag the edges or move the
frame, then click outside to save and deselect. **Escape** cancels; expand the
crop edges to reveal the original image again.
Copy selected elements with **⌘C** / **Ctrl+C**, cut with **⌘X** / **Ctrl+X**,
and paste with **⌘V** / **Ctrl+V**, within the same canvas or into another
thread. Copies preserve styles and layout; Undo removes a pasted group in one
step. Zoom and fit keep navigation simple.

## Capture a browser block

Desktop BB's built-in browser has a **Canvas** toolbar button. Hover to
highlight a block and click to capture its visible portion directly into the
thread's canvas. **↑** selects its parent; **Escape** cancels. Embedded frames
are captured as whole blocks. In web BB, paste or upload a screenshot instead.

## Show your agent

Agents can read saved element positions and text with **canvas_read**, or see
the entire board with **canvas_screenshot**, even when the panel is closed.
You can export the same view as a PNG. Newly installed tools are available on
the next agent session start.

## Saved per thread

The board saves locally on the BB server as JSON with separate images. Each
thread keeps its own canvas across panel closures and restarts. Failed saves
show **Retry** and retain a recovery draft across reloads in the current browser
tab when storage is available. Drafts stay isolated between tabs.
Deleting a thread removes its canvas. The board and its controls follow your
BB theme, light or dark, including San Francisco's accent colors.

plugins.description: Notes on elements of a page in BB's Browser: click an element, write a note, and send it to your agent as a pill with a screenshot.
plugins.overview:
Point at the part of a page you mean. Click an element in BB's Browser, write
a note, and your agent gets the note with a screenshot of the element.

## Notes on the page

Press **⇧⌘A** or choose **Annotate** in the Browser's toolbar, then click an
element. A note opens beside it; **Enter** adds the note and ends the pick. A
numbered pin marks the element, and a pill such as `1 · Buy Pro` appears in
the composer. Press the shortcut again for the next note, then send your
message. Click a pin to edit or delete its note. Change the shortcut in BB's
keyboard settings.
Needs the Browser of the BB desktop app, BB 0.46.0 or later.

## What your agent sees

Each pill gives the agent your note, the page's address, and the element's
selector, text, attributes, size, and main styles. It also gets a screenshot
of the page around the element, with the element outlined.

plugins.description: Keeps the plugins you pick up to date: BB checks for their updates every hour, day, or week and installs them.
plugins.overview:
Keep the plugins you pick up to date, without running `bb plugin update`.

## Pick the plugins

**Settings → Auto Update** lists every installed plugin that can take updates,
grouped by where it came from, like the app list in iOS Settings →
Notifications: BB Community, each marketplace you added, such as San Francisco
Plugins, and **Installed Directly** last. Each row shows the plugin's icon,
name, and version, with a switch that starts off. A switch that is on is your
consent: BB then installs that plugin's updates without asking.

## Choose how often

**Check for Updates**, at the top of the page, is every hour by default, or
every 6 hours, every day, or every week. **Check Now** checks every listed
plugin right away and installs the updates of those turned on. The page shows
when the last check ran.

An automatic install requires a change to the plugin's package version.
Commits to other plugins in the same repository do not reinstall an unchanged
version. The page shows **Version unchanged** for those candidates. If the
version cannot be verified, the update is skipped and the page shows why.
Authors must change their package version to ship an automatic update.
BB's own update badges and manual updates still use BB's update rules.

## See what happened

The list opens at once with what BB last knew, then each row checks its plugin
on its own and updates as the answer arrives, so a slow repository holds up
only its own rows. Each row says when an update is available or installing,
and when one failed, with the reason. It also says when an update needs a
newer BB, and when BB can't check the plugin for updates.

## BB's own updates

Auto Update installs updates the way `bb plugin update` does, so BB rolls back
a version that fails to start and shows its usual "Plugin updated" toast. Auto
Update updates itself last. Plugins that ship with BB update with BB, and
plugins pinned to a release tag, a commit, an exact npm version, or a local
folder never update, so the page leaves them out. No external account or
service is required.

plugins.description: See what fills your Mac's disk and clean archived threads, worktrees, dev caches, and the Trash.
plugins.overview:
See what fills your Mac's disk and clean what BB and your tools leave behind.

## See where space goes

**Settings → Storage Cleaner** shows the free space and a bar that splits the
disk into BB & agents, Dev caches, Apps, Trash, Your files, System, and free
space. Each category unfolds into its biggest items: archived threads by
title, leftover worktrees, caches, apps, and folders. Below, an explorer shows
the current folder as a treemap, with Contents, Largest files, File types, and
Stale tabs. **Customize rail** can put the same view in the sidebar.

## Clean a category

Every **Clean** asks first and lists what it deletes. BB & agents deletes the
storage of archived threads and the worktrees no live thread uses. Dev caches
empties Xcode DerivedData, package caches, git-ignored build folders, and
logs. Trash empties the Trash. Any file or folder can also be deleted from the
explorer.

## Every night

A scan runs every day at 00:00 UTC, and switches turn on cleaning threads
archived 7+ days ago, leftover worktrees, dev caches untouched for 7 days, and
the Trash. Sizes count APFS clones once, and a scan takes a few minutes.
Needs macOS and `python3`.

plugins.description: Live CPU, RAM, and GPU bars for the BB server in the sidebar, a page of its processes to sort, filter, and quit, and a guard that keeps BB responsive when the Mac is overloaded.
plugins.overview:
See how busy your BB server is from any page, without opening Activity Monitor
or `top`.

## Three live bars

The plugin's icon in the sidebar's navigation rail is three bars, CPU, RAM,
and GPU, that fill from the bottom and move every 2 seconds. A bar turns amber
at 85% and red at 95%.

## The numbers on hover

Hover the icon. In place of BB's tooltip, a small card shows each percentage
over a thin bar.

## A page of processes

Click or tap the icon for the Resources page. It shows the server's name and
uptime, the CPU model and core count, the RAM in use, and the GPU name. Below,
a list like Activity Monitor's shows the server's processes, with name, PID,
CPU, and memory. Click a column to sort by it, and filter by name, command
line, or PID.

## Quit what you don't need

Quit one process, or every process the filter shows. A dialog asks first, and
Force Quit stops a process that won't quit. BB's own processes are never
quit.

## Guard keeps BB responsive

On macOS, everything BB starts, agents and what they run, runs at a lower
priority than BB itself, so the app and the connection to your phone stay
quick when the Mac is overloaded. Under heavy load the busy ones run only on
the efficiency cores, and copies of the same command piling up are stopped.
Pause all on the Resources page stops BB's agents, what they run, and BB's
terminals until you resume them, from any device. Guard is a small separate
process that keeps working when BB is slow; turn it off in the plugin's
settings.

## Where the numbers come from

The BB server reads its own load every 2 seconds. RAM counts what Activity
Monitor calls Memory Used on macOS, and everything but available memory on
Linux. GPU load comes from macOS itself, or from `nvidia-smi` on machines with
NVIDIA GPUs. Processes come from `ps` on macOS and `/proc` on Linux, only
while the Resources page is open. Guard reads `ps` every 2 seconds and keeps
its state in its own folder. No external account or service is required.

plugins.description: A Slack button in every thread's header with your unread direct messages and mentions, which opens Slack in the right panel, or the Slack app on a phone.
plugins.overview:
See what waits for you in Slack from every BB thread, and open Slack beside
your work without leaving BB.

## A count in every thread

A Slack button in each thread's header shows your unread direct messages and
mentions, the same number as Slack's own badge. A dot means unread messages in
channels or threads you did not mute. The count updates every 20 seconds, on
your Mac and on your phone alike.

## Slack beside the thread

In the BB app, a click opens Slack in the thread's right panel, in BB's own
browser, which keeps you signed in. On a phone, it opens the Slack app.

## Set up once

The plugin reads the counts with your Slack session from a browser: its token
and its `d` cookie, which you paste into the plugin's settings. The README
shows where to find them. The BB server keeps them in a file only your user
can read and never sends them to a browser.

The counts come from the methods of Slack's web client rather than Slack's
public API, so a change at Slack can stop them until the plugin catches up.

plugins.description: BB's voice input transcribed on the BB server's Mac by Parakeet Ultra on the Neural Engine: 25 languages, no hesitations, and the audio never leaves the Mac.
plugins.overview:
Dictate to your agents with a speech model that runs on your own Mac.

## Voice input on the Neural Engine

The plugin transcribes BB's voice input with the Parakeet Ultra speech model
on the BB server's Neural Engine. The audio never leaves the Mac. A 10-second
take turns into text in about 0.3 seconds.

## 25 languages, no hesitations

The model finds the language on its own, among English, Russian, and 23 more
European languages, also mixed in one take. The plugin removes hesitations
such as "um" and "э-э".

## The built-in microphone, even with AirPods

Set Microphone to Built-in in Settings → Plugins → Voice Input. BB's voice
input then records with your Mac's, iPhone's, or iPad's own microphone, even
with AirPods or other headphones connected. Bluetooth headphones record worse,
so the built-in microphone transcribes better. The setting works with any
service that transcribes BB's voice input.

## Set up once

The BB server must run on a Mac with Apple silicon and macOS 15 or later, with
the Xcode Command Line Tools and ffmpeg. Pick Parakeet Ultra for voice input in
Settings → AI services. The plugin downloads the 350 MB model and gets ready on
its own.
